dct_description_sm: Mercury levels in predatory fish in inland lakes in the Mackenzie Valley have been reported to be increasing in recent years (Evans 2010). Evans reports: 'What is striking is the general tendency for mercury concentrations to be highest in the last year investigated with striking increases in Kelly Lake, Lac Ste Therese, and Cli Lake.' Cli Lake is in the Dehcho; other Dehcho lakes such as Deep, Sanguez, Tsetso, Little Doctor, McGill and Reade were reported to have elevated levels of mercury in predatory fish in earlier studies (Evans et al. 2005; Lockhart et al. 2005). Have mercury levels increased in these lakes as well? As relatively small lakes with large watersheds, this seems highly likely.                           Mercury levels in lake trout from Trout Lake have also increased over the last three testing periods to reach a level where Health Canada has issued a consumption advisory limit. The Sambaa Ke First Nation resides on the shores of Trout Lake and fishes for trout and walleye. Therefore, the project investigates whether mercury levels in walleye and lake trout have also increased.  The news of elevated levels of mercury in fish that appear to be on an upward trend was reported in the media which has resulted in concern in some Dehcho communities.  Thus there is an urgent need for updated mercury data on lakes in the Dehcho which are fished for food.   In partnership with Marlene Evans of Environment Canada, who will provide field protocol advice, lab analysis and interpretation of data, the Dehcho AAROM program will begin field work this winter collecting samples from the most important fishing lakes for six communities; Sambaa Ke (Trout Lake), Pehdzeh Ki (Wrigley), Jean Marie River, Liidlii Kue (Fort Simpson), Ka'A'Gee Tu (Kakisa), and  Deh Gah Gotie (Fort Providence).
